Lead — Iran Deadline / Ukraine Deep Strike

The Iran deal clock expired without a formal agreement

Polymarket's US–Iran permanent peace deal by May 31 prints at 4%, down from 8% a week ago; the Hormuz blockade-lifting contract dropped from 33% to 18% in 48 hours. In the same window Ukraine's SBU launched its most significant deep-strike package in weeks — drones destroyed two Tu-142 maritime patrol aircraft and an Iskander system at Taganrog airfield and struck the Feodosiya oil terminal in Crimea. Russia retaliated overnight with 290 drones and five Kh-101 cruise missiles; Ukrainian air defenses claimed 284 kills. Crimea began fuel rationing at 20 litres per person per day as of this morning.

Watch Areas — Configured Priorities

Israel–Iran–Hezbollah axis
High

The May 31 deadline passes without a deal. The Iranian ceasefire that held through May 24 has not been formally extended. Hegseth framed the US floor as denuclearization rather than full normalization; OFAC issued Counter-Terrorism Designations with an amended Iran-related FAQ within the past week.

Russia oil sanctions perimeter
High

The overnight strike on Taganrog port hits the watch-area bounding box directly. Burning a tanker and fuel terminal there signals Ukrainian capability to operate inside Russian coastal infrastructure; Crimea fuel rationing confirms downstream supply effects.

US tariff & trade dockets
High

The Federal Circuit emergency stay on CIT's Section 122 tariff invalidation is the week's outstanding ruling. CIT added three new opinions: ICON EV, Toyo Kohan, and Oregon v. United States — the first state-level tariff challenge at opinion stage.

Quiet today — Taiwan Strait · Korean peninsula · Critical minerals · EM debt · Sahel corridor · AI/semiconductor export controls · Latin America · Arctic.

Macro Situation

SOURCE — WORLDSCOPE LAKE · YIELD CURVE 2026-05-30
[ yield-curve chart ]

The US yield curve as of late May is no longer inverted at the front end; the 1-month to 1-year band sits around 3.62–3.85%, while the 10-year holds near 4.63%. The 90-day comparison shows the curve shifted down 10–20bp at the short end, consistent with markets buying a soft landing the data does not yet validate. [medium]

Oil is the primary macro transmission mechanism. Brent has settled into a $107–111 band since the jump to $115 when the conflict began February 28. Every dollar sustained above $100 for a quarter adds ~0.15–0.20pp to US CPI; at $109 for six months, roughly 0.9pp annually — preventing any Fed cut regardless of Warsh's stated preferences. [high]

Kevin Warsh's 54–45 confirmation on May 13 was the narrowest in modern Fed history. His record favors tighter policy than markets expect from a Trump appointee; the June 16–17 FOMC is his first test, priced for maximum ambiguity. [medium]
